answer: A slashable stake plus a reputation ledger resists sybils. To trade, an agent locks a deposit and earns limits only through verified work peers attest; cheating forfeits the stake. Like a river carving its channel only where water keeps flowing, trust grows slowly through repeated honest service, so a fake identity must sit through a long tundra of idle waiting before it can wander into high-value deals. Forging a thousand sybils then costs a thousand deposits plus months of upkeep, while one honest agent pays once, making the attack cost more than any reward it could extract.
